claims.text: After ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, the USING expressions of the table's policies are checked on every row a query by a non-bypassing role reads, before the query's own conditions; rows that fail are never seen.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.9 Row Security Policies; SQL command CREATE POLICY (USING)

claims.text: When row-level security is enabled on a table but no policy applies, a default-deny policy is assumed: no rows are visible or can be modified (customers in the demo counts 0).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.9 Row Security Policies ('default deny'); outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/row-level-security.txt last section

claims.text: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass row-level security; the table owner normally bypasses it too, unless the table is set to FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (not used here). A superuser passes every permission check.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.9 Row Security Policies; ALTER TABLE (FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY); CREATE ROLE (BYPASSRLS); 21.2 Role Attributes (superuser status)

claims.text: The official postgres Docker image creates the user named by POSTGRES_USER (here donhang) with superuser power; donhang creates, and so owns, the donhang_tenancy tables.
claims.source_hint: postgres Docker Official Image docs: Environment Variables, POSTGRES_USER; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml line 70, scripts/backend/tenancy-db.sh

claims.text: A PostgreSQL role is a user or group; SET ROLE changes the role the current connection acts as (a superuser may switch to any role). row-level-security.sql lines 9-16 create shop_app NOLOGIN and GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON orders, customers.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 21.1 Database Roles; SQL command SET ROLE; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 db/tenancy/row-level-security.sql lines 1-16

claims.text: A dotted name such as app.shop_id is a customized option PostgreSQL stores without interpreting, and any session may SET it to any value; current_setting(name, true) returns null instead of an error when it has never been set.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 19.16 Customized Options; 9.28.1 Configuration Settings Functions (current_setting missing_ok); SQL command SET

claims.text: ''::integer raises an error (invalid input syntax for type integer), so NULLIF is needed before the cast. That current_setting gives '' after a SET LOCAL has ended is attributed in the lesson to the comment in row-level-security.sql lines 20-21.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 8.1 Numeric Types, 4.2.9 Type Casts (integer input); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 db/tenancy/row-level-security.sql lines 20-21

claims.text: shop_id = NULL evaluates to null, not true (unlike C# ==), and a policy keeps only rows for which its expression returns true; NULLIF(x, '') returns null when x is the empty string.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators (null comparisons); 9.18.3 NULLIF; SQL command CREATE POLICY (false or null rows not visible)

claims.text: SET LOCAL lasts only until the end of the current transaction, whether committed or rolled back; plain SET lasts for the rest of the connection's session once its transaction commits (or when issued outside a transaction).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: SQL command SET (LOCAL, SESSION)

claims.text: The api's Npgsql driver (10.0.3, via Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL) pools connections by default, so one connection serves later requests; it resets session state on return by default, which No Reset On Close switches off; other poolers differ.
claims.source_hint: Npgsql docs: Connection String Parameters (Pooling, No Reset On Close); Basic Usage, connection pooling

claims.text: A policy FOR ALL applies to SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE; with no WITH CHECK, its USING expression is also used to check new and updated rows; a failing row gives ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "orders".
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: SQL command CREATE POLICY (ALL, WITH CHECK); outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/row-level-security.txt
